## How it works

- [statement] Do not use recurrence alone to discard potentially important minority cases: Anderson-Stanier explicitly notes that one-off insights can be compelling, and NN/G asks researchers to examine outliers and differences between participant groups when findings conflict. (medium confidence) — https://dscout.com/people-nerds/user-research-synthesis · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-research-findings/
- [statement] When evidence contradicts a theme, check how the studies were conducted before explaining away the difference. NN/g recommends examining participants, tasks, logistics and analysis, and warns against automatically overruling qualitative findings with quantitative results. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-research-findings/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Jobs-to-be-done frames the outcome a user seeks through a product. A job description can include circumstances and functional, emotional and social success criteria. Klement emphasizes situational motivations and anxieties when translating jobs into design work. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/personas-jobs-be-done/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.intercom.com/blog/using-job-stories-design-features-ui-ux
- [statement] Do not assume a one-to-one relationship between personas and jobs. NN/g notes that different user groups can have different requirements for the same job, while one persona can have different jobs in different contexts. Preserve these distinctions when turning themes into needs. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/personas-jobs-be-done/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use personas to express behavior, needs, goals and relevant context. Use jobs-to-be-done to express the outcome sought and the situation and motivations behind it; demographic attributes alone do not explain the job. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/personas-jobs-be-done/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.intercom.com/blog/using-job-stories-design-features-ui-ux

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Treat generated persona content as a representation requiring validation, not as observed human evidence: the conceptual analysis of generative personas describes convincing fabricated content as a hallucination risk, while NN/G requires persona characteristics to be grounded in real-user research. (medium confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1071581925002149 · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/persona/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Personas should synthesize research about real people rather than invent user evidence; the MOD case study explicitly excluded suspected personas that its research had not uncovered. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/persona/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://defencedigital.blog.gov.uk/2021/05/17/understanding-online-working-in-defence-the-importance-of-personas-in-user-research/
- [statement] Klement criticizes attribute-based personas for failing to explain causality and proposes Job Stories; Laubheimer argues that behavioral personas and JTBD are compatible. These are attributed practitioner positions rather than proof of a universal replacement rule. (medium confidence) — https://www.intercom.com/blog/using-job-stories-design-features-ui-ux · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/personas-jobs-be-done/
- [statement] When findings contradict a theme or each other, NN/G recommends checking participants, tasks, logistics and analysis before interpreting the difference; it recommends triangulating self-reported and observed evidence rather than following requests verbatim. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-research-findings/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Coding categorizes raw data. Inductive codes develop after reviewing data; deductive codes are defined before synthesis. Anderson describes goals, needs, motivations, tasks and pain points as useful categories in her workflow, rather than a mandatory taxonomy. (low confidence) — https://dscout.com/people-nerds/user-research-synthesis · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Use personas as research-derived decision aids rather than replacements for research with people. NN/g explicitly cautions that persona-based expert reviews should not replace user testing. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/persona/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Keep observation, interpretation and action distinct: record what participants said or did, group similar observations into themes, write findings for the groups, and attach proposed actions. Coding and grouping help connect raw evidence to recommendations. (medium confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/analyse-a-research-session · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://dscout.com/people-nerds/user-research-synthesis
- [statement] GOV.UK recommends grouping observations into themes, splitting overly broad groups, and attaching findings and proposed actions to their relevant groups so the reasoning remains connected to the observations. (low confidence) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/analyse-a-research-session · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Klement proposes identifying a high-level job and smaller contributing jobs, observing the current solution, formulating Job Stories around causality, motivations and anxieties, then creating a feature or interface solution. His article illustrates this workflow with one team’s profile-page design. (low confidence) — https://www.intercom.com/blog/using-job-stories-design-features-ui-ux · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] The persona-visualization study reports that presentation influenced persona perception and could somewhat reduce stereotyping; its sample consisted of computer-science students, so the finding does not establish that personas eliminate bias across professional design teams. (low confidence) — https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3340764.3340771 · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done
- [statement] Personas represent fictional people but must draw their substantive characteristics from research about real users. Research-based behaviors, attitudes and goals are central; irrelevant biographical detail should not displace information that informs design decisions. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/persona/ · keywords: UX research synthesis, personas and jobs-to-be-done · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/personas-jobs-be-done/
